sections.heading: The Box Customers Keep on Their Dresser
sections.text: Keep-Forever Packaging The Box Customers Keep on Their Dresser Most jewelry packaging gets opened once. A leather drawer organizer gets used every day — your logo sitting on the customer's dresser for years. That retention is why boutique jewelry brands are moving from throwaway boxes to organizer-grade packaging. The shell is rigid board wrapped in stitched PU leather (rose, black, tan, sage or custom), with a drawer that glides on tuned tolerances — firm enough to stay shut in a handbag, smooth enough to open with one finger. Inside, suede-lined compartments hold rings, earrings and bracelets in configurable layouts. Deboss your logo in gold on the lid, add a mirror under the top face, or pair with our velvet presentation box for gift-then-keep programs. See the full jewelry packaging range .

sections.heading: PU, PVC or Microfiber — and Why It Decides Your Logo
sections.text: Material Decision PU, PVC or Microfiber — and Why It Decides Your Logo "Leather" on a jewelry box is almost always one of three synthetics, and the one you pick quietly sets the ceiling on how your logo can be applied. PU PVC Microfiber Hand Soft, matte, closest to everyday leather goods Firmer, takes high gloss Closest to genuine hide Foil stamping Accepts foil and digital print well Narrow heat window Accepts foil, deepest deboss hold Deep embossing Moderate Handles deep emboss and gloss lamination Excellent, holds edge definition Relative cost Mid Lowest Highest Typical fit Most jewelry and watch programs Budget retail display Flagship / heirloom positioning The practical difference shows up at the foil press. Published guidance for embossing faux leather puts PU at roughly 110–140 °C and PVC at roughly 90–120 °C , with 2–6 bar pressure and a dwell of 0.5–2.0 seconds. That narrower PVC window is the whole story: too cool and the foil reads blurry and patchy, too hot and the surface glazes or blisters — and PVC reaches "too hot" sooner. If your logo is a fine serif wordmark or has hairlines under about 0.3 mm, specify PU or microfiber and give the press room to work. Save PVC for solid, chunky marks where a degree of spread does not hurt. Material thickness follows the same logic as bookbinding, where 0.6–0.8 mm is the normal range for covers . Thinner than that and the board telegraphs through at the drawer edge; much thicker and the drawer sleeve loses clearance and starts to bind.

sections.heading: Drawer Clearance: the Half-Millimetre That Decides the Feel
sections.text: Structural Detail Drawer Clearance: the Half-Millimetre That Decides the Feel A drawer box is judged in the first second, by how the tray slides. Too tight and the customer tugs and the sleeve bows; too loose and it coasts out in transit and the contents rattle. That feel is a clearance spec, not a craftsmanship mood. The tray runs inside the sleeve with a deliberate gap on each side — tighten it and the covering material's own thickness eats the tolerance, which is exactly why the leather choice above is not just cosmetic. A 0.8 mm wrap on a tray that was toleranced for 0.6 mm removes clearance from both walls at once, and a box that passed on the dieline binds in production. Three things we lock at sampling, and that you should check on any supplier's sample before bulk: Pull test with the tray loaded. An empty tray always feels fine. Load it to the real weight of your piece and pull — the sleeve should not flex visibly at the mouth. Inverted test. Hold the closed box upside down and shake once. A correctly toleranced drawer stays put through friction alone; if it drops, the fix is clearance or a ribbon pull, not tape. Cycle it thirty times. Synthetic leather burnishes where it rubs. If a shine line appears along the sleeve mouth after thirty open-and-close cycles, the fit is too tight for a box customers will actually reuse. The ribbon pull tab is worth a line of its own: it exists so the customer's fingers never grip the tray face, which is where fingerprints and edge wear otherwise concentrate. On a box positioned as keep-forever, that tab is doing more work than it looks like it is.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions Is the leather real or vegan? Stitched PU (vegan) leather as standard — consistent grain, animal-free, and colour-matchable. Genuine leather is available on request from 500 pcs. How smooth is the drawer action? Drawer tolerances are tuned to ±0.5mm: firm enough to stay closed in a handbag, smooth enough to open one-handed. Every sample is glide-tested before approval. What compartment layouts are possible? Ring rolls, earring pads, bracelet channels, watch pillow and open trays — mixed per your collection. Layouts are die-cut per order, not off-the-shelf. Can you add a mirror inside the lid? Yes, a glass mirror bonded under the lid face is a stocked option and adds roughly $0.40–0.60 per unit at 500 pcs. What is the MOQ? 100 pcs in stocked colours (rose, black, tan, sage, ivory); custom Pantone leather starts at 300 pcs.
